02.title: General knowledge
02.prompt: Why does temperature control matter when making chocolate?
02.before: Complete milestone 02: activate the prepared BasicChatComponent, implement createChatClient in chat.ts and enable the backend chat service. Restart the backend launcher, reload the app and start a fresh conversation.
02.expected: An ordinary explanation based on general knowledge, without claiming to have inspected this factory.
02.inspect: Trace POST /api/chat to the OpenAI client and completion call written live in chat.ts. Explain that conversation works before facility access exists.

02.title: Expose the missing data connection
02.prompt: What is the current air temperature in our Cooling room?
02.before: Keep the same conversation. Do not paste readings into the chat.
02.expected: The assistant should explain that it cannot access current facility readings. Any invented temperature is a failed demonstration, not evidence of access.
02.inspect: Compare with the real snapshot. The backend route supplies no facility tools or live readings.

03.title: Streaming conversation
03.prompt: Why does temperature control matter when making chocolate?
03.before: Complete chapter 03, restart the backend launcher, and reload Angular at localhost:4200. Open the AG-UI Chrome extension panel again before sending the prompt.
03.expected: The answer arrives progressively and uses general knowledge, without claiming access to this factory.
03.inspect: Show the AG-UI Chrome extension again: run-start, text-delta and run-finish events. Inspect /api/copilotkit requests and the AG-UI run-start, text-delta, and run-finish events. Compare with the single JSON response in chapter 02.

03.title: No frontend tools yet
03.prompt: Show only warnings from the Cooling room.
03.before: Keep the snapshot or reading log visible and note the current filters.
03.expected: The application filters remain unchanged. The model has no frontend tools; a textual claim of success is not an application action.
03.inspect: Show that BuiltInAgent has a model and static prompt, with no tools connected. Mastra is introduced in chapter 04.

04.title: One agent, two entry points
04.prompt: Why does temperature control matter when making chocolate?
04.before: Start Mastra API on 4211 and Studio on 4212. Show the default agent in Studio and try the prompt there. Restart the chapter-4 backend, then send the same prompt in a fresh Angular conversation on 4200.
04.expected: Both entry points produce a general explanation. Angular streams through CopilotKit to the Mastra agent. Neither answer claims to inspect live factory data.
04.inspect: Required: show Mastra Studio, its agent model and instructions, then the trace corresponding to the Angular request. Also show the unchanged CopilotChat and the new MastraClient adapter.

04.title: Hosting does not grant data access
04.prompt: What is the current air temperature in our Cooling room?
04.before: Keep the actual facility snapshot visible. Do not paste readings into chat.
04.expected: The assistant should explain that it cannot access current readings. An invented temperature fails this demonstration.
04.inspect: Show tools: {} in the Mastra agent and the static prompt. Explain that frontend tools are introduced in chapter 5.

05.title: Discover options through Angular
05.prompt: Which rooms and shift managers are available?
05.before: Open a fresh Angular conversation on 4200 after completing chapter 5. Show the AG-UI Chrome extension.
05.expected: Calls list_rooms and list_shift_managers and reports only the names returned by Angular.
05.inspect: Show empty input objects, array results and the matching manual filter options. This uses tool results, not reactive agent context.

05.title: Operate the existing controls
05.prompt: Switch to the reading log and show only warnings from the Cooling room managed by Charles Bond.
05.before: Keep the previous conversation so discovered IDs are available. Keep the view buttons and filters visible.
05.expected: The reading log is selected and room, manager and warning filters match the request. Existing unrelated filters are preserved.
05.inspect: Inspect set_view and set_filter_values, their returned results, and the actual controls. Compare handlers with the methods used by the template.

05.title: Change one date without losing other filters
05.prompt: Change only the start date to now.
05.before: Keep the room, manager and warning filters from the previous demo.
05.expected: Only the start boundary changes to the browser current time. No matching readings is a valid result.
05.inspect: The tool arguments omit unrelated fields. Angular preserves them and resolves the now convention.

05.title: Clear exactly one field
05.expected: The start date clears; room, manager and condition remain selected.
05.inspect: Show from: null and explain that null clears that field while omission preserves the others.

05.title: Tools still have a data boundary
05.prompt: What is the current air temperature in our Cooling room?
05.before: Keep actual readings visible but do not paste them into chat. Open Mastra Studio on 4212 to inspect an Angular trace.
05.expected: The assistant explains that it cannot read measurements with these tools.
05.inspect: Show the Angular request trace in Studio. Room and manager discovery plus UI control do not grant historian access; Studio standalone chat has no Angular handlers.

06.title: Discover the exact metric
06.prompt: Which metrics are available in the Cooling room?
06.before: Complete chapter 06, wait for Angular and Mastra to reload, and start a fresh Angular conversation on 4200. Open the AG-UI Chrome extension. Clear old filters and select Snapshot.
06.expected: Calls list_metrics and reports metrics belonging to the Cooling room using the returned names. It makes no measurement claims.
06.inspect: Show the returned exact metric IDs, names and room names. The handler returns options, not readings.

06.title: Reject an alarm proposal
06.prompt: Raise an alarm for the Cooling room air temperature because I observed a cooling failure.
06.before: Use a target without an active alarm. If necessary, use the existing manual acknowledge/resolve controls. Keep Snapshot and the audit visible.
06.expected: The raise_alarm tool renders a proposal card. No alarm is created before approval. Click Reject: the audit records rejected and not-executed; the assistant acknowledges rejection without retrying.
06.inspect: Show the tool arguments and the operator decision separately. Inspect the correlation ID and authoritative outcome in the audit and tool result.

06.title: Approve and verify execution
06.prompt: Raise an alarm for the Cooling room air temperature because I observed a cooling failure.
06.before: Repeat the request after rejection. Confirm the target still has no active alarm. Click Approve and raise alarm on the new proposal.
06.expected: The alarm appears in Snapshot. The audit records approved, executed and the created alarm ID; the assistant confirms the returned outcome. A failed execution must be reported as a failure.
06.inspect: Show the AG-UI result and the Angular request trace in Mastra Studio on 4212. Compare the trace with the durable facility audit. Selecting a checkpoint does not undo this alarm.

07.title: Read historical measurements
07.prompt: Show the latest ten air-temperature readings from the Cooling room.
07.before: Complete chapter 07, wait for Mastra and Angular to reload and start a fresh Angular conversation on 4200. Keep backend 3101 running and open the AG-UI Chrome extension.
07.expected: Calls query_historian once with the whole question. Successful stored readings open in the Historian result grid. The assistant receives a completion receipt, not the row values.
07.inspect: Show the question-only tool input and the full tool result in AG-UI. In Studio on 4212, inspect the registered workflow and the Angular request trace: generate SQL, semantic review, deterministic validation/execution.

07.title: Select the stored maximum rows
07.prompt: Show the highest air-temperature reading for each shift manager.
07.before: Keep the same conversation and the historian grid visible. Use existing stored readings; selecting a checkpoint does not reset them.
07.expected: Returns complete stored reading rows for the maxima, including manager and timestamp, using the same fixed table. The previous historian result is filtered out of later model input.
07.inspect: Compare SQL, returned rows and the grid. Show toModelOutput and ToolCallFilter: Angular retains full results while the main model gets only the receipt. Switch to Snapshot and back to Historian result to show result retention.

07.title: Expose the fixed-table limit
07.prompt: What is the average air temperature in the Cooling room?
07.before: Keep the fixed result grid visible. This checkpoint does not support aggregate result shapes.
07.expected: Explains that averages are unsupported in this chapter. The assistant may decline without calling a tool; if it calls the workflow, an unsupported aggregate must not be executed as a successful grid result.
07.inspect: Explain that model refusal alone does not prove SQL validation. Show the prepared backend policy or local tests for that boundary. Use this limitation to introduce A2UI in webinar 08.

08.title: Display aggregate data in a generated table
08.prompt: Show a table of the average air temperature for each room. Include only the room name and average temperature.
08.before: Complete chapter 08, restart pnpm dev:backend, wait for Angular and Mastra reload and start a fresh Angular conversation on 4200. Open the AG-UI Chrome extension.
08.expected: Calls query_historian with the complete request, obtains aggregate data and displays an A2UI table using the requested columns. The same widget also appears in chat; this is accepted for the webinar.
08.inspect: Inspect SQL, returned values and A2UI activity. Show the prepared catalog and compare the generated table with chapter seven’s fixed reading grid. The assistant receives a receipt, not row values.

08.title: Choose columns without editing Angular
08.prompt: Show the latest ten air-temperature readings from the Cooling room in a table with only time, temperature and shift manager.
08.before: Keep the same conversation and the main generated view visible. The previous result payload is filtered before another request reaches Mastra.
08.expected: The generated table contains the requested columns and stored reading values without a template change. No second display tool is needed.
08.inspect: Compare query rows, component configuration and rendered cells. Show HistorianBridge, toModelOutput and ToolCallFilter as the prepared result-handling boundaries.

08.title: Compose repeated cards and tables
08.prompt: Show one card per room, with a table of its latest five air-temperature readings. Include time and temperature.
08.before: Use the same Angular conversation. Open Mastra Studio on 4212 for the Angular request trace. Ask explicitly for cards and tables to select the UI branch.
08.expected: Composes room cards with tables bound to real data. The main area and chat both render the widget. Verify the result rather than relying on the assistant’s acknowledgement.
08.inspect: Show select-result-format and generate-a2ui in Studio, plus AG-UI activity. The format agent receives metadata; the composer receives the question and columns, while application code binds the actual rows.
